surfaces.part: hanging shirts (pink, green, lilac) and the two dark shirts inside the ring

answer.evidence: The top ring is an ellipse. The width profile goes 14,20,24 at the back rim, widens to 28 at row 9, then narrows through 26 and 22. It has a bright front-rim line at row 10 with a shadow row below it. The base is also an ellipse: widths 10,16,18,18,16,12 over rows 26-31, with a light highlight line at row 28. The central pole is visible in rows 24-27 and the hanging garments fill rows 12-23. Both the horizontal ring and the base therefore show top faces above a front face of well over 3 rows. The garments count as hanging goods (decor).

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are fine: 14 visible tones per tile sits between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and the well (20), and near-flat coverage is 0%. The problem is craft. 78% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the grey-black outline around the ring top and pole reads as a sticker line. Beodeul's props with material-tinted outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%) don't look like that; only the metal lamp pole is fully neutral. The garments and the glass-like top ring have only about 3 lightness steps each (base, a light tone and a shadow), against 5-6 on the references. They have little grain or per-item highlight work. The piece is clean and readable but flatter and thinner than the stall and well beside it, and with this much doubt it fails.

answer.evidence: This is a round clothing rack. The top ring widens from 14 to 28 px and narrows again, with a light front-edge line at row 10 (#f3f4f7) and a shadow row at 11, so it reads as an ellipse seen from above. The base is also an ellipse: widths go 10, 16, 18, 18, 16, 12 over rows 26-31, with a light front-edge line at row 28. The central pole between them (rows 12-25) is the vertical front face. The hats in the ring and the shirts on the rack are goods and count as decor. Both horizontal frame parts show top faces.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 14 visible tones per 16x16 tile, inside the reference range (hedge 9, stall 17, well 20), and 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. The garments show about 3-4 lightness steps each, with fold shading and highlights, and the glass top and rack have a few grey steps. That is slightly fewer than Beodeul's 5-6, but it is a small, sparse prop. The dark edges are 78% near-neutral, which leans towards a grey outline. The prop-lamp-crook reference is 100% neutral on a metal pole, and on the picture the garment edges look like darker pastel tones rather than a uniform black sticker line, so I call the outline mixed. Texture is moderate: fold and highlight dots but little grain. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the references, since it does not look noticeably thinner or flatter than the bench or lamp.

surfaces.part: top hanger ring (elliptical ring with bright front rim)

answer.evidence: The rack has an elliptical hanger ring at the top. Its width profile goes 14, 20, 24, then 28, with a bright front rim at row 10 and shadow below. The base is an ellipse of rows 26-31 with widths 10, 16, 18, 18, 16, 12, and a bright front-rim row at 28. Both horizontal frame parts therefore show top surfaces. The shirts hang between them as decor goods, and the pole at rows 24-26 is a vertical support. The front face and legs together span about 15 rows, so the object reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small clothes rack with a round top and pastel garments. Its density is decent: 14 visible tones per tile against 17 for the stall and 20 for the well, with 0% near-flat coverage. The problems are outline and shading. 78% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, much closer to the lamp (100%) than to the hedge (0%), stall (1%) or well (33%), which carry material-tinted edges. The dark grey/black line around the rack and garments reads as a sticker outline, not a dark tone of the neighbouring material. Each material ramp is shallow: the garments and grey metal frame show about 3 steps each, against 5-6 on the references. Only 19 distinct colours in total, against 38-40 for the stall and well, leaves little per-material grain or per-item highlighting. The garments are simple blocks with little fold texture. It is clean and readable, but a careful artist would see it as flatter and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small round-topped clothes rack with pastel garments. Its measured density is fine: 14 visible tones per tile, between the hedge (9) and the stall (17) and well (20), with 0% near-flat coverage. The weak points are shading and outline. 78% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and stall and 33% for the well. That reads as a grey/black sticker-style outline rather than a dark tone of each neighbouring material. The garments look like only about 3 steps each (base, light, dark), with little grain or per-item highlight, and the rack top and stand look like a flat grey with a thin highlight. At this size it holds up next to the bench and lamp, but not next to the richer stall and well, which have tinted outlines and 5-6 steps per material. The neutral outline plus shallow ramps tips it to fail; metal, as on the lamp, might partly justify the grey edges, but the garments do not.
